Refers to images created of objects in the UMMAA collections.
The attribution for the source of the image; a photographer taking an image of an UMMAA object

This subcategory includes activities related to the construction of buildings and other features, such as mounds, canals, or graves. Acquisition of building materials (stone quarrying, felling wood) is classed as Activity- Technology/manufacturing.
This subcategory is applied to everyday activities carried out at the level of the household or small work parties.

item.value: Activities: Food production/Animal or Plant Husbandry

label.name_singular: Activities: Food production/Animal or Plant Husbandry
label.name_plural: Activities: Food production/Animal or Plant Husbandry
label.description: This subcategory includes all activities related to food production with the exception of cooking. Activities related to care of livestock, hunting, gathering, gardening and agricultural production, as well as scenes of initial processing are included.
This subcategory includes all activities and objects related to the practice of healing and medicine
An image that depicts people buying, selling, trading, or exchanging goods.

This subcategory includes all activities related to ritual and religion, including both public and private rites, as well as preparation of ritual materials. If the activity has both religious and secular components, code as both.

This subcategory is applied to communal, secular events held in public or semi-public contexts. If the event depicted can have both secular and religious components (ex. some feasts, potlatch), code as both.

This subcategory is applied to activities involved in the manufacture and processing of tools and other objects (but not structures or features). It includes all steps of the manufacturing process, including acquisition of raw materials.
An image that depicts people traveling or transporting goods, such as animal caravans, canoeing, etc.
This subcategory includes all rockshelters, rock overhangs and caves with evidence of human use.

This subcategory is applied to images depicting the distinctive layout or architecture of entire large towns or cities, as well as representations of significant portions of towns or cities. (Compare with Arch-Village)
This subcategory is applied to images depicting individual defensive features such as walls, ditches or moats, as well as the variety of defensive settlement types.
This subcategory includes structures and additive features (cemeteries, burial mounds) dedicated to the processing, disposal, and honoring of the dead.

item.value: Architecture: House or other domestic structure

label.name_singular: Architecture: House or other domestic structure
label.name_plural: Architecture: House or other domestic structure
label.description: This subcategory includes images of all types of habitations, whether extant or archaeological, complete or partial.
This subcategory includes all constructions involved in the manufacture or processing of food or other objects. Quarries are not included (see Cultural Landscape- Lithic Raw Material Source).

This subcategory includes large, unroofed and generally unmovable monuments constructed of one or more large stones. Items may be undecorated or exhibit modification in the form of sculpture, incising, etc. Potential overlap w/ Art-sculpture.

This subcategory includes mounds built by the accretion of houses and living surfaces or by intentional construction with clean soil and/or trash deposits. When they can be distinguished, funerary mounds are not included in this category.
This subcategory includes non-habitation buildings or constructed spaces that are the loci of primarily secular public activities, such as commerce, communal gatherings, and performances.
This category includes buildings or building complexes believed to house royalty. Palaces or palace complexes may also include administrative and religious buildings.

This subcategory includes buildings or constructions (such as altars or shrines) that are the loci of ritual activities. Note potential for overlap with several of the Art subcategories and the Architecture - megalith/monument subcategory.

This category includes free-standing facilities or separate rooms used exclusively for the storage of food, water, livestock or other items. Storage features found w/in rooms, such as sub-floor pits or bins, are classed in the Feature-storage subcategory.
This subcategory includes buildings or other constructions whose purpose is unknown, not specified by the image or description, or does not fit into the other architecture categories.

This subcategory includes images that depict the distinctive architecture and layout of entire villages or clusters of buildings. Regional terms for villages or building clusters may be specified in the detail field.

This subcategory includes walls that are not clearly part of larger constructions/buildings or fortifications. Images which show close-ups of wall construction should be classed in the Feature - wall/wall construction subcategory.

Includes features made from stone or other materials designed to control water flow from runoff, waterways or other sources. Constructions designed for water storage (ex. cisterns, wells, reservoirs) are included in the architecture-storage subcategory.
Includes elements of buildings that exhibit some sort of distinctive form/shape or decorative elements. May overlap with Art-sculpture subcategory.

Includes paintings and some bas relief sculpture found on the walls of caves, especially paintings dating to the Upper Paleolithic. May overlap with Art - Rock Art given regional traditions of naming.

This subcategory includes large-scale designs created by either the addition (e.g. creation of rock alignments, mounding of earth) or subtraction (e.g., removal of desert pavement or sod) of rock, soil, or vegetation.
This subcategory includes later "additions" to architectural features or artworks (such as rock art panels) which were not envisioned by the original artist.

This subcategory includes all wall and floor art created by painting or inlay. "Fresco" can be applied to paintings on wet or dry plaster. Choice of mural or fresco can be based on local naming conventions.
This subcategory includes images of artwork created by the application of paint to various media.

Includes small, readily portable objects that have been sculpted/engraved/incised and/or decorated with paint or inlay (note potential overlap w/artifact - religion). Items with a clear function but w/ "artistic merit" (ex. painted shields) are included.

Includes designs or representations executed on rock outcrops or boulders either by the application of paint (pictograph), pecking away of rock (petroglyph), or incision with (usually) metal objects (incised designs).

Includes free-standing, relatively unmovable and "attached" (to architecture) items that have been sculpted, carved, engraved, or incised with either geometric or representational designs. May overlap with Art- Arch. Elements. No portable objects.

label.description: Includes images depicting large-scale modification of the landscape through creation of fields, gardens, terraces, orchards.

item.value: Cultural Landscape: Raw material source- clay

label.name_singular: Cultural Landscape: Raw material source- clay
label.name_plural: Cultural Landscape: Raw material source- clay
label.description: Includes locations on the landscape where clay is procured.

item.value: Cultural Landscape: Raw material source- lithic/mineral

label.name_singular: Cultural Landscape: Raw material source- lithic/mineral
label.name_plural: Cultural Landscape: Raw material source- lithic/mineral
label.description: Includes locations on the landscape where lithic raw material was collected or excavated for use in the production of stone tools or metallurgy.

item.value: Cultural Landscape: Raw material source- other

label.name_singular: Cultural Landscape: Raw material source- other
label.name_plural: Cultural Landscape: Raw material source- other
label.description: Includes locations on the landscape where raw materials other than stone and clay are acquired.

Includes long-distance or aerial images of sites and their environmental/topographic setting. Also includes landscape shots taken from sites (but not showing portions of the site itself) showing the distinctive features of the location.
An image of an animal used as a burial offering.
This subcategory includes depictions of whole or partial in situ burials of one or more animals.
This subcategory includes images of living, recently dead, stuffed or otherwise reconstructed animals.
This subcategory includes images of the skeletal remains of animals.
This subcategory includes images that demonstrate the osteological differences between species and between fauna of different sex and age.

Includes images of features in which deceased humans or animals have been deposited. Does not include architectural constructions for disposal of the dead (Architecture-Funerary). Note potential for overlap with Human Remains- burial/cremation(s).

Includes depictions of floors or other surfaces, either in horizontal exposure or in profile. Non-archaeological floors (in use) with distinctive characteristics are also included in this subcategory.
Includes deposits that contain discarded artifacts and materials and may contain discarded ash, charcoal, or food remains (shell, bone). Note potential for overlap with Feature-profile/strata.
This subcategory includes features that do not fit any of the other Feature subcategories or features whose function is unknown (with the exception of pits of unknown function).
This subcategory includes soil stains interpreted as the remains of decayed, burnt or removed architectural posts.
This subcategory includes images of stratigraphic profiles, as well as closeups of individual strata. Note potential for overlap with Feature-floor and Feature-midden.

This subcategory includes features that functioned as storage facilities, as well as pits of other (ex. smudging) and unknown function. Does not include thermal features such as roasting pits and smudge pits).

Includes all features associated with retaining fire or heating food and other items. Accumulations of fire-cracked or fire-altered rock (FCR) are included in this subcategory. Constructions (ex earth ovens, kilns) are classed in the Architecture category
This subcategory includes features associated with transportation (by humans, animals, boats, variety of engine driven machines).

Includes images of walls or associated features that focus on wall construction (ex. bldg materials, masonry styles, wall trenches, etc.). Images of walls that don't emphasize wall construction may be classed in the Architecture category.

Includes earthen features designed to control water flow from runoff, waterways or other sources. Constructions designed for water storage (ex. cisterns, wells, reservoirs) are included in the architecture-storage subcategory.
Includes depictions of wood charcoal and of unburned wood. Does not include non-wood charcoal.
Includes depictions of coprolites, particularly those which demonstrate their macro- or micro-botanical content.
The partial or whole remains of a corn cob.
Includes depictions of the remains of fruits, whether charred or uncharred.
Includes depictions of the remains of nuts, whether charred or uncharred.
Includes depictions of phytoliths.

item.value: Flora- Archaeological: Plant fibers, tissues, and epidermis

label.name_singular: Flora- Archaeological: Plant fibers, tissues, and epidermis
label.name_plural: Flora- Archaeological: Plant fibers, tissues, and epidermis
label.description: Includes depictions of plant fibers, tissues, and epidermis, whether charred or uncharred.
Includes depictions of pollen.
Includes depictions of the remains of seeds, whether charred or uncharred.

item.value: Fossil Hominids/Physical Anthropology: archaic Homo sapiens

label.name_singular: Fossil Hominids/Physical Anthropology: Archaic Homo sapiens
label.name_plural: Fossil Hominids/Physical Anthropology: archaic Homo sapiens
label.description: Includes depictions of (non-Neanderthal) archaic Homo sapiens, the remains of archaic Homo sapiens, or objects/environments/features associated with this species. H. heidelbergensis IS included, but Neanderthals have a separate subcategory.
Includes depictions of Australopithecines, the remains of Australopithecines, or objects/environments/features associated with this species. Zinjanthropus is another name for A. boisei.
Includes depictions of Homo erectus, the remains of Homo erectus, or objects/environments/features associated with this species. Includes H. ergaster and early specimens called Pithcanthropus.
Includes depictions of Homo habilis, the remains of Homo habilis, or objects/environments/features associated with this species.
Includes depictions of modern humans or characteristics of modern humans which illustrate principles of physical anthropology.
Includes depictions of Neanderthals, the remains of Neanderthals, or objects/environments/features associated with this subspecies.
This subcategory is a catch-all for depictions that cannot be placed into the other subcategories.
This subcategory includes all images with either multiple hominid species or unidentified hominid species
Includes depictions of one or more skeletal elements either of fossil hominids, or of ethnographic or modern humans that illustrate principles of physical anthropology.
This subcategory includes images of geographic features, vegetation communities, and fauna characteristic of desert environments.
This subcategory includes images of geographic features, vegetation communities, and fauna characteristic of grassland environments.
This subcategory includes images of mountains, escarpments, and other structural features.
Includes images of sunsets and sunrises.

item.value: Geographic Feature: Temperate and boreal forests

label.name_singular: Geographic Feature: Temperate and boreal forests
label.name_plural: Geographic Feature: Temperate and boreal forests
label.description: This subcategory includes images of geographic features, vegetation communities, and fauna characteristic of temperate and boreal forests.
This subcategory includes images of geographic features, vegetation communities, and fauna characteristic of tropical environments.
This subcategory includes images of geographic features, vegetation communities, and fauna found in the tundra.
Highly remarkable or unusual natural feature such as a natural bridge or gyser.

item.value: Geographic Feature: Volcanic, tectonic and glacial features

label.name_singular: Geographic Feature: Volcanic, tectonic and glacial features
label.name_plural: Geographic Feature: Volcanic, tectonic and glacial features
label.description: This subcategory includes geographic features created by glacial, tectonic, or volcanic activity. Excludes mountain ranges, even if created by volcanic or tectonic activity (use Geographic Feature - Mountain(s)/escarpments).

item.value: Geographic Feature: Waterbodies and associated landforms

label.name_singular: Geographic Feature: Waterbodies and associated landforms
label.name_plural: Geographic Feature: Waterbodies and associated landforms
label.description: This subcategory includes images of waterbodies such as lakes, oceans, and estuaries and the variety of landforms that may be associated with them (ex. beaches, deltas)

item.value: Geographic Feature: Waterways and associated landforms

label.name_singular: Geographic Feature: Waterways and associated landforms
label.name_plural: Geographic Feature: Waterways and associated landforms
label.description: This subcategory includes images of waterways such as springs, creeks, braided streams, and rivers and the variety of landforms that may be associated with them (ex. floodplain, levy, remant terrace)
This subcategory includes images of complete or partial, in situ or reconstructed burials of one or more human beings.
mummy
This subcategory is applied to images that depict osteological manifestations of human pathologies, including injuries.
This subcategory is applied to images that depict the osteological characteristics that distinguish the sexes.
This subcategory is applied to images that depict one or more individual human skeletal elements.
This subcategory includes all maps that show the distribution of sites or isolated artifacts (ex. Clovis points) over a large area. Depictions of artifact density over large areas are also included.
This subcategory includes all maps that depict site plans, whether the individual components of the map are artifacts or buildings.

Includes both general maps that depict a mix of topography and/or geographic features such as rivers and mountains, etc. AND maps with more restricted themes (such as volcanoes, soil type distributions, precipitation or temperature distributions, etc.)
This subcategory includes all maps depicting the distribution of culture areas (prehistoric and historic) or language groups/dialects.
Images in this subcategory depict physical anthropologists engaged in research in a laboratory setting. Examples of unique kinds of phys anth data are included.
Images in this subcategory depict physical anthropologists engaged in field research.
Images in this subcategory depict ethnologists engaged in field research.

label.name: Ranking
label.description:
Condition Ranking 1:
High priority for treatment; actively deteriorating.
This may include:
• major structural problems
• mold/mildew
• active corrosion on more than 25% of surface
• flaking/lifting/powdering/ spalling or friable surface, more than 25%
• active tearing/breaking
• major insect damage/ live bugs

Condition Ranking 2:
Needs remedial treatment; condition may worsen quickly over time.
This may include:
• active corrosion less than 25% of surface
• broken due to failed adhesive
• old restorations/failing restorations
• deteriorated coatings
• flaking/lifting/powdering/spalling or friable surface, less than 25%
• needs new housing

Condition Ranking 3:
May benefit from or require treatment to improve appearance; condition is stable with little potential for active deterioration.
This may include:
• accretions
• dirt
• dust
• losses
• old restorations

Condition Ranking 4:
No treatment necessary; condition is stable.

Condition Ranking 5:
No treatment is possible; deterioration is
irreversible/irreparable, and/or object is
disintegrated/unsalvageable

label.name: Geographic Location
label.description: This field corresponds to the largest common name associated with the artifact, image, or site related to a natural feature. This field differs from Political Location in that it refers to more natural features on the landscape. Common entries include: river valley, mountain range, desert, plains etc.

label.name: Political Location
label.description: This field is used for specific town names, village names, or other identifiable locales. This field differs from Geographic Location in that it refers to more man-made features or designations.

label.name: Where Collected?
label.description: In some instances, objects have been collected at a specific place such as a market, store, ceremonial gathering. This information should be included here. If the only information you have is a town, village or similar name, it should be placed in the “Political Location” field.

label.name: Where Manufactured?
label.description: Some objects will be collected in one region of the world but actually manufactured in another. Although this information will also be included in the description field, specifics can be added to here for searching purposes. For example: The Guthe collection was collected in the Philippines, but many of the ceramic vessels were manufactured at specific kilns in Thailand or China. The kiln name, province, country should be added here.

label.name: Provenience
label.description: The field corresponds with the provenience information associated mainly with excavated materials. This can include mound numbers, unit numbers, test pit numbers, elevation, and anything else that has been used to identify the actual provenience of an object. For objects excavated at large sites such as Mound 34, Cahokia. The overall site name (Cahokia) should be entered into the Archaeological Site Name field and Mound 34 should be added to the Provenience field

label.name: Specific Name
label.description: This field is used for scientific names or type names. Examples include: Sus barbatus (for domestic pig); Stanley Tool Impressed (pottery type), Barton Incised (pottery type). It is not used for names such as plainware, redware, bison, horse, etc. These non-specific names should be included in the description.
